title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and request timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: continuous batching scheduler has shown intermittent starvation for low-priority short requests under mixed workloads and occasional head-of-line blocking when long requests delay batch formation. Motivation: reduce starvation events, improve per-priority fairness, and make timeouts adaptive to observed queueing dynamics without regressing throughput.

Summary of changes: implemented per-priority queue aging (priority_boost) that incrementally increases effective priority for requests waiting beyond an age threshold; added a fairness quota allocator that enforces soft max share per priority window to prevent starvation of lower-priority traffic; introduced adaptive per-priority batch formation timeouts computed from recent batch formation latency (exponential moving average) with configurable floor/ceiling; bounded per-priority queue lengths and a probabilistic early-drop policy for overloaded queues; fixed a race condition in scheduler shutdown where pending timers could reschedule batches; added new telemetry and alerts.

Why this approach: aging + soft quotas preserves throughput-optimal batching while preventing pathological starvation observed in mixed short/long workloads. Adaptive timeouts avoid one-size-fits-all values across models and request size distributions. Early-drop prevents queue blowups on noisy tails.

Benchmarks/results: microbenchmarks on p4d nodes with synthetic mix (70% short chat, 30% long completion) show p99 tail latency reduction for short requests by ~18% and 40% fewer starvation events across a 1-hour stress run. End-to-end throughput was within 2% of baseline; median latency unchanged. Canary in prod (10% traffic) ran for 48h before rollout.

Testing: unit tests for scheduler heuristics, integration tests simulating mixed workloads, added deterministic timing tests for timeout logic, and end-to-end canary harness.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout: start 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with SLO monitoring on batch_wait_seconds, starvation_events, fairness_skew. If starvation_events drop <10% improvement or fairness_skew increases >15%, rollback.

review_comments: Diego Martínez: Nice approach — can you clarify how the priority_boost affects the batching invariant? Concerned about churn if boosts oscillate.

Ava Chen: Priority_boost is additive to the effective priority and decays after a batch is formed; we use a bounded boost and EMA to avoid oscillation, added comments and unit tests to validate non-oscillation scenario.
Priya Kapoor: Please add dashboards and a runbook entry for the new starvation_events metric so SRE can triage quickly.
Ava Chen: Added dashboard json in docs and included runbook steps in ops doc. Marked for SRE review.

Ethan Liu: Found a race where shutdown cancels timers after a new batch is scheduled; this can reschedule stale timers. Please ensure timer lifecycles are owned by the scheduler with proper cancellation token.
Ava Chen: Reworked timer ownership model, added a cancellation token and corresponding tests. Thanks for the catch — updated tests and CI.
Diego Martínez: CI failure was an unrelated flaky integration; reran and everything is green. Approving for merge.
Priya Kapoor: Approved — validated dashboards and rollout plan.
Ethan Liu: LGTM after fix, approving.
release_notes: Improve continuous batcher scheduler: per-priority aging to prevent starvation, adaptive batch timeouts, bounded queues with early-drop to avoid queue blowups, new telemetry (batch_wait_seconds, starvation_events, fairness_skew). No breaking changes. Rollout controlled by feature flag.
test_plan: Unit tests + integration harness added. Ran 48h canary at 10% traffic and synthetic stress tests. CI integration retried once due to known flake. Recommend standard canary rollout and monitor batch_wait_seconds, starvation_events, fairness_skew, and per-priority queue depth metrics.
notes: Related PRs: pr-18399 (earlier scheduler fairness work), pr-21087 (timeout heuristics prototype). This PR consolidates those approaches and hardens shutdown behavior.
